clue.text: Melon Jack found in a Spanish house

indicators.note: the sailor is found inside the house, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: casa is the Spanish word for a house
a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: A cook discovers a melon kept in a house in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name, but in crosswords a jack is a sailor; 'found in' puts him inside the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A casaba is a variety of winter melon with wrinkled yellow skin.

clue.text: Church painter who wanted parliamentary reform

parts.note: a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: A painter of church scenes who also campaigned for reform of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a British working-class movement of the 1830s-40s demanding votes for all men and other reforms of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the nineteenth-century People's Charter movement campaigned for changes such as universal male suffrage.

clue.text: Guide carries a minute cooking utensil

indicators.note: the guiding word carries the other pieces inside it like a load

parts.note: to guide is to steer

explanation.surface: A guidebook features a tiny kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like 'tiny' but is the unit of time, M.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a pan with a perforated insert for cooking food over boiling water.

clue.text: Before spring newly-wed goes to prison

indicators.note: the newly-wed is placed ahead of the spring in the word

parts.note: a bride is a woman newly married
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A newly married person ends up in jail before the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but it is a water source, WELL. Bridewell was a London house of correction whose name came to mean any jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell, from a London jail, became a general word for a lock-up or house of correction.

clue.text: Devotee of tailored suits

indicators.note: suits is read as the verb: the letters are fitted or arranged to suit a new word

explanation.surface: Someone who adores well-cut tailored suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suits' looks like clothing, completing the tailoring picture, but it tells you to rearrange TAILORED.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater is a worshipper of idols, and loosely any ardent admirer.

clue.text: Couturiere who schemes to get her man

definitions.text: who schemes to get her man

explanation.surface: A fashion designer plotting to catch a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A couturiere is literally a woman who designs clothes; a scheming female plots and manipulates for a husband.

clue.text: Meadow Way is most insignificant

parts.note: a lea is a meadow in poetry
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A path across a meadow is the least important route.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, the smallest in importance.

clue.text: End up getting a set of clothes

explanation.surface: Finishing up with a new outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn out is to result or end up; a turnout is also one's dress or equipment, an outfit.

clue.text: Managing to give a judicial decision

explanation.surface: Running things so as to deliver a court's verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling means governing or controlling; a ruling is also a court's formal decision.

clue.text: Diana's date was a let-down

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, plus the possessive S
a date is an appointment

explanation.surface: Diana's romantic evening was a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'date' suggests romance; here it is simply an engagement, APPOINTMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A disappointment is something that fails to meet hopes, a letdown.

clue.text: Gents in top-quality neckwear need good features

indicators.note: the gents are placed in the top-quality term

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 written as the letter I
gents are men
ties are worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Men wearing smart ties need some redeeming qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top-quality' is A1, with the figure 1 standing in for the letter I, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are pleasant or useful facilities, the attractive aspects of a place.

clue.text: A month in Capri left us restored

indicators.note: the month is found sitting in the run of letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A month on the island of Capri left us refreshed.
explanation.walkthrough: The month is buried in 'cAPRI Left'; 'us restored' only completes the holiday picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month of the calendar year, between March and May.

clue.text: Casual worker has time for painting

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An office temp takes time off to paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a technique using pigment bound in egg yolk, and a picture done that way.

clue.text: Swallowed with difficulty when depressed

explanation.surface: Gulping something down while feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: To get food down is to manage swallowing it; to get someone down is to make them miserable.

clue.text: Merry frolic for couple in diocese

indicators.note: the couple sits in the diocese word

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
PR is an abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: A married couple enjoy a fun outing within a bishop's district.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree is a lively bout of fun or indulgence.

clue.text: In a monastery it takes precedence

indicators.note: the word it is placed in the religious house

parts.note: a priory is a monastery ruled by a prior

explanation.surface: In a religious house, one thing comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Priority is the right to come first, being ranked ahead.

clue.text: Furious about a member running amok

indicators.note: the furious word goes about, surrounding, the other pieces

parts.note: furious means raging
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An angry MP goes on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampaging means rushing about violently, out of control.

clue.text: Induce a director to be successful

parts.note: to induce someone to do something is to get them to
a head is a director or leader

explanation.surface: Persuading a boss to help you prosper.
explanation.definitionFit: To get ahead is to make progress and succeed in life or career.

clue.text: Suggesting that I am working steadily

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
plying a trade is working at it steadily

explanation.surface: Hinting that one is hard at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to hint or indicate without saying outright.

clue.text: Mother made trial of wedlock

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: the word trial is made into something new by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Mum tested out married life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' tells you to rearrange TRIAL into RITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital means relating to marriage.

clue.text: Syrup producer is a soft-hearted fellow

indicators.note: the fellow has the soft element at his heart, in the middle

parts.note: a male is a fellow or man
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A kindly man who makes sweet syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft-hearted' reads as 'kind' but means P (soft) at the heart of MALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugar maple's sap is boiled down to make the familiar pancake syrup.

clue.text: Confidential talk around teatime

indicators.note: the talk goes around the time piece

parts.note: to prate is to chatter or talk idly
tea is traditionally at four o'clock, IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A secret chat over afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Teatime is four o'clock in British custom, so the Roman IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Private means secret, not for public knowledge.

clue.text: Small carp stink

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A little fish that smells bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' might suggest complaining, but it is the fish family, here the tench.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, foul smell.

clue.text: Exhaust and metal wheel-rim inaccurately placed

parts.note: a tire is the metal band round a cartwheel, the older spelling of tyre
out means wrong or inaccurate, as in a guess being out

explanation.surface: A badly fitted metal rim on a car exhaust.
explanation.definitionFit: To tire out is to wear someone out completely, to drain their energy.

clue.text: To upset a woman further

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word to on its head, reading upward

parts.note: taken as written
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Distressing a woman even more.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean additional or further, as in 'other matters'.

clue.text: Old air can be produced on it

definitions.text: Old air can be produced on it

indicators.note: the letters are produced afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: An instrument for playing old tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be produced' signals the anagram of the two middle words; read whole, the clue also describes what the instrument does.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument on which simple melodies can be played.

clue.text: Nick is anything but a companion

parts.note: not is the plain negative, anything but
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: Nick is a lonely soul with no friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name; it is the definition, a small cut. CH is the British honour Companion of Honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, a nick.

clue.text: I created a disturbance to remove all traces

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs the letters of I created and a into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to causing trouble and wants to wipe out the evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy something completely, root and branch.

clue.text: Gaiety of Italian during term at Oxford

indicators.note: Italian comes during, inside, the term word

parts.note: Hilary is the Oxford University term from January to March

explanation.surface: The merriment of an Italian student at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford's three terms are Michaelmas, Hilary and Trinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is loud mirth and merriment.

clue.text: Generally admitted to be a gourmand's weakness

parts.note: a gourmand loves food, and greed is the failing of overeating

explanation.surface: Everyone accepts that greed is a glutton's flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed means accepted by common consent.
